# When the runs of a process settle

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`when-the-runs-of-a-process-settle` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F04 · [record](when-the-runs-of-a-process-settle.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> In a world a list holds, some run of a process keeps changing exactly where a reachable change can be undone; that no run keeps changing does not give settling, which is the limited principle of omniscience already for two configurations.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. A run that changes within a loop, between two visits of one configuration, gives a run from the same configuration that goes round the loop and keeps changing; a run that keeps changing does not settle. (`Becoming.Settling.ChangeRecurs`, `Becoming.Settling.ChangesInLoop`, `Becoming.Settling.not_settles_of_recurs`, `Becoming.Settling.roundIndex`, `Becoming.Settling.roundIndex_lt`, `Becoming.Settling.roundIndex_last`, `Becoming.Settling.roundIndex_le`, `Becoming.Settling.roundIndex_back`, `Becoming.Settling.roundIndex_from`, `Becoming.Settling.roundIndex_hits`, `Becoming.Settling.round`, `Becoming.Settling.round_recurs`, `Becoming.Settling.recurs_of_loop`)
2. Along a run whose configurations a list holds, change that recurs is a change within a loop. (`Becoming.Settling.extend`, `Becoming.Settling.extend_le`, `Becoming.Settling.extend_gt`, `Becoming.Settling.rising`, `Becoming.Settling.changes_at`, `Becoming.Settling.loop_of_recurs`)
3. In a world a list holds, some run from a configuration keeps changing exactly where some run from it changes within a loop, exactly where a configuration reachable from it has a step to another configuration from which it can be reached again; where every run settles, or assured enough holds, there is no such step. (`Becoming.Settling.undoable_of_loop`, `Becoming.Settling.consSeq`, `Becoming.Settling.consAct`, `Becoming.Settling.path_seq`, `Becoming.Settling.path_then`, `Becoming.Settling.recurs_of_undoable`, `Becoming.Settling.keeps_changing_iff_loop`, `Becoming.Settling.keeps_changing_iff`, `Becoming.Settling.settles_no_undoable`, `Becoming.Settling.assured_no_undoable`)
4. Not changing for ever is not settling: with two configurations and no way back from the second, no run keeps changing, and every run from the first settling is the limited principle of omniscience. (`Becoming.Settling.OneWay.process`, `Becoming.Settling.OneWay.seen`, `Becoming.Settling.OneWay.run`, `Becoming.Settling.OneWay.seen_stays`, `Becoming.Settling.OneWay.seen_witness`, `Becoming.Settling.OneWay.no_undoable`, `Becoming.Settling.OneWay.never_keeps_changing`, `Becoming.Settling.OneWay.lpo_of_settles`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom. A process and a configuration; a list holding the run or the world where stated.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- Settling without the limited principle of omniscience: with no reachable undoable change, every run settling is exactly LPO for every process of decidable configurations in a world a list holds (the-last-change-of-a-run).
- Worlds no list holds, where change can recur without a loop (how many times a run changes within a list is in the-last-change-of-a-run).
- **Counterexample:** OneWay: two configurations with no way back from true; no run keeps changing, and every run from false settling gives LPO (OneWay.lpo_of_settles). [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Settling.lean)

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps. · A law of the formal model; its correspondence to actual systems is a separate obligation. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision. · A relation omitted by a weaker description does not refute the fuller account.
